cond_0001.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting, experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission through working to build a government acquisition capability, and work to support the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizen who meets specialized experience requirements
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4 years experience in contracting or related positions, with at least 1 year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower level
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management
At least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13, including: experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; and experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics
Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service
Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed)
Preferred Requirements
Contracting/Procurement knowledge: knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration
Leadership and Teamwork: influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations; encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals
Communication: expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information; makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

cond_0132.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0132.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, staying in regular contact with stakeholders to strengthen the acquisition workforce and ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, actively advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare and communicate various formal and informational materials to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate is a motivated, self-reliant, and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission by helping build a strong government acquisition capability and working closely with the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0132.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizen who meets specialized experience to qualify
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4 years experience in contracting or related positions, with at least 1 year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower level
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management
At least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13, including: experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND experience performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics
Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service
Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed)
Preferred Requirements
FAC-C certification with program/project management experience
Familiarity with the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system
Experience or desire to grow into acquisition policy formulation and oversight
Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (e.g., Federal Acquisition Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration
Demonstrated leadership and teamwork: influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations; encourages cooperation, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit
Strong communication skills: expresses information to individuals or groups effectively, makes clear and convincing presentations, listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

cond_0169.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0169.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program.
Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision.
Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives.
Contribute to the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance.
Prepare various formal and informational communications to internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate is a motivated, self-reliant, and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have strong analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will support DOT's mission by helping build a strong government acquisition capability and supporting acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0169.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen and meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service.
GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only.
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizenship
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4 years experience in contracting or related positions, with at least 1 year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower level
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management (exceptions and waivers apply per agency policy)
At least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13 level, including: experience as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures, providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND experience performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices
Contracting/Procurement knowledge: familiarity with various contract types, techniques, and requirements (e.g., Federal Acquisition Regulations), contract negotiation, and administration
Communication: ability to convey information clearly to individuals or groups, accounting for audience and subject matter; clear written and direct verbal reporting
Preferred Requirements
Experience documenting findings and sharing written documentation with senior-level leadership on procurement-related topics
FAC-C certification with program/project management experience
Familiarity with the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system
Leadership and Teamwork: ability to influence and work with others toward shared goals, foster cooperation and team commitment, and adapt approach to different situations
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Contribute to the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communications to internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant, and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have strong analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will support DOT's mission by helping build a capable government acquisition function and supporting acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0196.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen & meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service. GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only. PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND (3) meet either the education or experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.
To qualify for the GS-14, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13. It must include:
Experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND Experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND Experience documenting findings and sharing written documentation with senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas:
Contracting/Procurement - Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration. Leadership and Teamwork - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
For additional information about applying to Federal positions, please click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-policies/#url=e4
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Education
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4-years experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience must have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, and must have provided the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the work of the position.
And
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
Additional Information
FLSA Exempt
This announcement may be used to fill additional positions if similar vacancies occur within 90 days of the issue date of the referral certificate.
Qualified CTAP/ICTAP candidates receive priority and will be referred to the hiring manager.

[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0224.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Lead DOT's acquisition workforce program, taking ownership of strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Execute delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and deliver recommendations for decision. Plan, direct, and conduct on-site training/briefings to improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Drive the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Produce various formal and informational communications to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will lead the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to advance DOT's mission by building a strong government acquisition capability and supporting the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0224.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizen who meets specialized experience to qualify
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4 years experience in contracting or related positions, with at least 1 year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower level
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management
At least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13, including: experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics
Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service
Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed)
Preferred Requirements
Technical knowledge of contracting/procurement: knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration
Leadership and Teamwork: influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations; encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals
Communication: expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
For additional information about applying to Federal positions, please click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-policies/#url=e4
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Education exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
This announcement may be used to fill additional positions if similar vacancies occur within 90 days of the issue date of the referral certificate.
Qualified CTAP/ICTAP candidates receive priority and will be referred to the hiring manager.

cond_0229.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting, experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of federal acquisition policy and procurement processes.
cond_0229.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
cond_0229.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen & meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service. GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only. PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND (3) meet either the education or experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.
To qualify for the GS-14, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13. It must include:
Experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND
Experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND
Experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas:
Contracting/Procurement - Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration.
Leadership and Teamwork - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.
Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Education
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4-years experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience must have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, and must have provided the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the work of the position.
And
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.

cond_0239.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting, experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission through working to build a government acquisition capability, and work to support the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
Most people become stronger in this kind of acquisition and policy work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0239.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
cond_0239.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen & meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service. GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only. PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizenship
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4-years experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience must have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, and must have provided the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the work of the position.
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. (See waiver and exception provisions below.)
To meet the minimum qualifications for GS-14, at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13, including: experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
Copy of transcripts submitted for verification
Preferred Requirements
FAC-C certification with program/project management experience
Familiarity with the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system
Technical Skills — Contracting/Procurement: Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration.
Leadership and Teamwork: Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.
Communication: Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.
Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0312.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, staying in regular contact with stakeholders to strengthen the acquisition workforce and ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, actively advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare and communicate various formal and informational materials to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate is a motivated, self-reliant, and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission by helping build a strong government acquisition capability and working closely with the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0312.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
U.S. Citizen who meets specialized experience to qualify
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4 years experience in contracting or related positions, with at least 1 year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower level
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management
At least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13, including: experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND experience performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics
Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service
Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed)
Preferred Requirements
FAC-C certification with program/project management experience
Familiarity with the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system
Experience or desire to grow into acquisition policy formulation and oversight
Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (e.g., Federal Acquisition Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration
Demonstrated leadership and teamwork: influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations; encourages cooperation, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit
Strong communication skills: expresses information to individuals or groups effectively, makes clear and convincing presentations, listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Own DOT's acquisition workforce program lead function, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program.
Execute delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision.
Plan, lead, and deliver on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives.
Drive the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance.
Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
cond_0323.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen & meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service. GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only. PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND (3) meet either the education or experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.
To Qualify For The GS-14, You Must Have At Least One Year Of Experience Equal Or Equivalent To The GS-13, It Must Include
Experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND
Experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND
Experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas:
Contracting/Procurement - Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration.
Leadership and Teamwork - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.
Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
For additional information about applying to Federal positions, please click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-policies/#url=e4
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Education
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4-years experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience must have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, and must have provided the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the work of the position.
And
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4. Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
Additional Information
FLSA Exempt
This announcement may be used to fill additional positions if similar vacancies occur within 90 days of the issue date of the referral certificate.
Qualified CTAP/ICTAP candidates receive priority and will be referred to the hiring manager.

cond_0324.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0324.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Coordinate with DOT's acquisition workforce as the program lead, working alongside colleagues to strengthen the acquisition workforce and support effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program.
Share delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and contribute recommendations for decision.
Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings together with relevant teams to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives.
Participate collaboratively in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance.
Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate is a motivated, skilled professional who will help support the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work alongside DOT's acquisition professionals across the Department to help build a strong government acquisition capability.

[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0426.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting, experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission through working to build a world class government acquisition capability, and work to support the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
cond_0426.requirements:
You must be a U.S. Citizen and meet specialized experience to qualify. Submit application and resume online by 11:59 PM EST on the closing date. Required documents must be submitted by the closing date. Direct Hire Authority will be used to fill this position.
SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service. GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only. PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
To meet the qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND (3) meet either the education or experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.
To qualify for the GS-14, you should have around one year of experience equivalent to the GS-13, ideally including:
Experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND Experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND Experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
Volunteer work, unpaid experience, and work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social) all count toward qualifying experience. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas:
Contracting/Procurement - Working knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration. Leadership and Teamwork - Ability to influence, motivate, and work with others; openness to adapting your approach to different situations. Encourages cooperation, trust, and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Communication - Ability to communicate effectively with individuals or groups, taking into account the audience and nature of the information; willingness to listen to others and respond appropriately.
EDUCATION: Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including around 4 years of experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience should have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, providing the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the work of the position.
And
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management.
Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4.
Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
This announcement may be used to fill additional positions if similar vacancies occur within 90 days of the issue date of the referral certificate.
Qualified CTAP/ICTAP candidates receive priority and will be referred to the hiring manager.

SELECTIVE SERVICE: Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered for the Selective Service.
GOVERNMENT TRAVEL CARD: This position involves travel. A government contractor-issued travel card will be issued and must be retained for official business only.
PROBATIONARY PERIOD: Applicants may be required to successfully complete a one-year probationary period (unless already completed).
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND (3) meet either the education or experience qualifications for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.
To qualify for the GS-14, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-13. It must include:
Experience serving as a subject matter specialist for a range of contracting procedures and providing oversight to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and guidance documents, performing policy interpretation, and providing advice and recommendations to team members, management, and stakeholders; AND
Experience in performing procurement process reviews and documenting best practices; AND
Experience presenting findings and written documentation to senior level leadership on procurement related topics.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas:
Contracting/Procurement - Knowledge of various types of contracts, techniques, or requirements (for example, Federal Acquisitions Regulations) for contracting or procurement, and contract negotiation and administration.
Leadership and Teamwork - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals.
Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.
Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
For additional information about applying to Federal positions, please click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-policies/#url=e4
All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.
Education
Completion of all mandatory training prescribed by the head of the agency for progression to GS-13 or higher level contracting positions, including at least 4-years experience in contracting or related positions. At least 1 year of that experience must have been specialized experience at or equivalent to work at the next lower level of the position, and must have provided the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the work of the position.
And
A 4-year course of study leading to a bachelor's degree, that included or was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the following fields: accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management.
Exceptions: Employees in GS-1102 positions will be considered to have met the standard for positions they occupy on January 1, 2000. This also applies to positions at the same grade in the same agency or other agencies if the specialized experience requirements are met. However, they will have to meet the basic requirements and specialized experience requirements in order to qualify for promotion to a higher grade, unless granted a waiver under Paragraph 4.
Waiver: When filling a specific vacant position, the senior procurement executive of the selecting agency, at his or her discretion, may waive any or all of the requirements of Paragraphs 1 and 2 above if the senior procurement executive certifies that the applicant possesses significant potential for advancement to levels of greater responsibility and authority, based on demonstrated analytical and decision making capabilities, job performance, and qualifying experience. With respect to each waiver granted under this Paragraph 4, the senior procurement executive must document for the record the basis of the waiver. If an individual is placed in a position in an agency on the basis of a waiver, the agency may later reassign that individual to another position at the same grade within that agency without additional waiver action.
Additional Information
FLSA Exempt
This announcement may be used to fill additional positions if similar vacancies occur within 90 days of the issue date of the referral certificate.
Qualified CTAP/ICTAP candidates receive priority and will be referred to the hiring manager.

cond_0469.intro:
This position is located in [Location masked], Acquisition Policy, Oversight and Business Strategies Division.
[Company name masked] is responsible for ensuring that the Department's acquisition business processes operate efficiently and effectively and are responsive to the needs of their customers and advance DOT's strategic goals.
cond_0469.responsibilities:
The Procurement Analyst Will
Serve as DOT's acquisition workforce program lead, strengthening the acquisition workforce to ensure effective management of the Department's acquisition workforce career program. Perform delegated DOT Acquisition Career Manager (ACM) responsibilities as directed by supervisor, advise the DOT ACM on relevant acquisition workforce related matters, and make recommendations for decision. Plan, coordinate, and conduct on-site training/briefings to generally improve the overall acquisition function or to provide information on the latest acquisition developments as they apply to specific DOT contracting issues and/or initiatives. Participate in the development of departmental acquisition policy and guidance. Prepare various formal and informational communication to both internal and external audiences on acquisition related topics.
The ideal candidate for this position is a motivated, self-reliant and skilled professional who will assist in leading the Department's acquisition policy function in an effective, efficient, and ethical manner. The ideal candidate will have excellent analytical, writing, and oral communications skills. These skills should accompany a broad range of experience in the contracting profession, including a combination of operational contracting, experience and/or desire to grow into the acquisition policy formulation and oversight arena.
The candidate should maintain FAC-C certification with program/project management experience and be well versed in the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) [Product name masked] system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to support DOT's mission through working to build a government acquisition capability, and work to support the hundreds of acquisition professionals across the Department of Transportation.
